newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude in corrective down phase.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude in corrective down phase.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures slipped lower on Monday in what chart analysts said was a technical correction to earlier gains.

April NYMEX crude slipped 37 cents a barrel to close at $20.92 a barrel, while April heaing oil lost nearly a cent to end at 54.30 cents a gallon. Gasoline was around half a cent per gallon weaker at 65.26.
"It looks like yesterday's trade was just a correction," said one Washington-based chartist.
She said the low reached on March 12 at $19.86 a barrel was significant support because it amounted to a key reversal pattern. "It looks as though we have the low in the market now."
She also saw support, based on the 19-day moving average, at $20.80 and said that was the first hurdle if the market was to test further downwards.
"But I expect we will see some choppy trading," she said, and added that the market may test lower, perhaps even down to $19.86, before recovering.
"Heating oil and unleaded (gasoline) have all made key reversal patterns and they are all trying to do some building."
Gasoline was supported at Monday's low of 64.60 cents and she said she was looking out for a break above 66.25, the level of Monday's high and just below the high of this month's range at 66.30.
The market needed to conquer that level to continue moving constructively, she said.
"We need to make a new high in terms of that (66.25) level and we need to get above that level if we are going to get this thing going," she said.
GNI analysts said in a daily report they saw significant resistance at $21.50 for April NYMEX crude and added they expected some volatility in the market.
"WTI (NYMEX crude) posted an inside day which is a sign of indecision," they added.
MeesPierson Derivatives said they saw support at similar levels to those the chartist mentioned above.
"We managed to hold in the support test at $20.84 which suggests a day of range activity."
"Only a break of $19.80 would put us on the defensive.
